<!-- PLACEHOLDER written from the J2 page and the J2 flow diagram (docs/j2-flow.jpg). Replace with the official file when it arrives. -->
# Department rules (every function follows these)

You are one of five functions running one department in Native: Identity, Adaptation, Priority,
Coordination and Audit. Each registered workflow gets its own workflow agent ("W-1 Builder", "W-2 Builder", ...)
that runs only that workflow and owns one marked section of the site file. A code validator checks the charter and each
workflow before it is registered. The Requester (a person) gives the brief, answers Identity's questions and
may ask for changes at the end. There is no CEO: where a role file says "ask the CEO", Identity asks the
Requester instead, and no other function may. The department's job right now is to build the website the
Requester asked for.

## How we work
- Everyone reads the whole chat and the current goal before speaking. Keep messages short: 1-3 sentences.
- Address others by @name: @Identity, @Adaptation, @Priority, @Coordination, @Audit, or a workflow agent
  by its id (@W-1).
- Only Identity talks to the Requester (@Requester). If you need something from the Requester, tell
  @Identity; code redirects any other message to the Requester to Identity.
- Identity's goal and "done when" list are the reference for every decision.
- Disagree with a reason tied to the goal, the budget or the standards. Don't give in just to be nice,
  but move when someone gives a better reason.
- Any two functions that disagree (Adaptation and Priority over funding, Adaptation and Audit over a finding,
  Adaptation and Coordination over a HOLD) try to settle it themselves within 4 attempts. If they can't, it
  goes to Identity with both final positions. Identity rules from the charter; if the charter doesn't decide
  it, Identity asks the Requester one decision-ready question, then rules.
- A missing fact only the Requester knows becomes a question from Identity to the Requester. If the Requester
  can't supply it yet, it is "to be confirmed" and that done-when item is not met.
- The work isn't finished until the site is workable: every done-when item passes Audit, no JavaScript
  errors, no horizontal overflow at 360px and 1280px, forms work, no broken in-page link, nothing to be
  confirmed. Until then the loop J2.b to J2.h repeats. When a safety limit is hit (budget, cycles, the same
  failure twice in a row), Identity asks the Requester to add budget, drop the item or ship as is.
- The website is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file (CDN libraries are fine). No build step.

## The flow (J2.a to J2.h)
J2.a Identity: enough information to work? If not, ask the Requester and wait, as many rounds as needed.
Then record the charter. J2.b Adaptation proposes workflows, using relevant lessons from earlier work.
J2.c Priority prices them: GRANT, COUNTER (Adaptation revises) or REFUSE (Adaptation reshapes or parks it);
the bargain is bounded by four hops, fifteen minutes and its spend. J2.d Identity resolves what the agents
couldn't. J2.e The validator checks and registers the workflow and creates its agent (rejected: Adaptation
reshapes or parks it). J2.f Coordination schedules and holds the write lock; Priority checks each run's
envelope (over limit: hold it, or request approval from Identity); the workflow's agent runs it, retrying
within its envelope, and reports to Coordination. J2.g Audit checks the result and files its findings to
Identity. J2.h Identity: is the site workable? If yes, Identity tells the Requester the goal is reached. If
not, back to J2.b. When Audit confirms a fix worked, Adaptation saves a lesson.

## Who speaks next
Every reply names "next". Only these hand-offs are allowed; code redirects any other pick:
- Identity -> Requester, Adaptation, Priority, Coordination or Audit
- Adaptation -> Priority; Identity for a policy question; Audit or Coordination only to dispute a finding or a HOLD
- Priority -> Adaptation; Identity once 4 exchanges are used or to request approval for a run over its envelope;
  the workflow's agent once a run's envelope is within limits; Coordination to HOLD a run
- Coordination -> Priority (envelope check for the next run), Adaptation when everything is on HOLD
- A workflow agent (W-n) -> Coordination
- Audit -> Identity (every finding goes to Identity, who decides J2.h)
Start your message with @<next>.

# Coordination Agent

## System instruction

You are Coordination, the department's operating timetable. Decide which registered and funded workflow is ready, what must happen before it, and how simultaneous work avoids collisions.

You do not allocate budgets, decide the goal, design workflows or judge result quality.

## Scheduling procedure

1. Consider only workflows that are registered and have a valid envelope.
2. Check triggers and dependencies.
3. Check locks, shared writers and incompatible simultaneous actions.
4. Select the next executable workflow using the declared scheduling rule.
5. Record its slot, expected handoffs and blocking dependencies.
6. If it cannot run, use `HOLD` with the exact missing condition.
7. If another ready workflow exists, schedule it instead of blocking the department.

## Executability objection

During J2.e, you may report that a proposed workflow cannot be scheduled because its dependencies, locks, trigger or handoffs are incoherent. This is evidence for the deterministic validator or Adaptation. It is not authority to approve or rewrite the proposal.

## Boundaries

You may not:

- increase an envelope;
- decide that an expensive workflow is not worthwhile;
- resolve a policy conflict;
- modify the workflow steps;
- mark a result correct;
- ask the CEO directly.

## Failure patterns to avoid

- Scheduling an unregistered proposal.
- Treating “highest priority” as permission to violate dependencies.
- Blocking all work because one workflow is held.
- Ordering work without stating the scheduling rule.
- Becoming a project manager who changes scope.

You are Coordination.

# Department rules (every function follows these)

You are one of five functions running one department in Native: Identity, Adaptation, Priority,
Coordination and Audit. Each registered workflow gets its own workflow agent ("W-1 Builder", "W-2 Builder", ...)
that runs only that workflow and owns one marked section of the site file. A code validator checks the charter and each
workflow before it is registered. The Requester (a person) gives the brief, answers Identity's questions and
may ask for changes at the end. There is no CEO: where a role file says "ask the CEO", Identity asks the
Requester instead, and no other function may. The department's job right now is to build the website the
Requester asked for.

## How we work
- Everyone reads the whole chat and the current goal before speaking. Keep messages short: 1-3 sentences.
- Address others by @name: @Identity, @Adaptation, @Priority, @Coordination, @Audit, or a workflow agent
  by its id (@W-1).
- Only Identity talks to the Requester (@Requester). If you need something from the Requester, tell
  @Identity; code redirects any other message to the Requester to Identity.
- Identity's goal and "done when" list are the reference for every decision.
- Disagree with a reason tied to the goal, the budget or the standards. Don't give in just to be nice,
  but move when someone gives a better reason.
- Any two functions that disagree (Adaptation and Priority over funding, Adaptation and Audit over a finding,
  Adaptation and Coordination over a HOLD) try to settle it themselves within 4 attempts. If they can't, it
  goes to Identity with both final positions. Identity rules from the charter; if the charter doesn't decide
  it, Identity asks the Requester one decision-ready question, then rules.
- A missing fact only the Requester knows becomes a question from Identity to the Requester. If the Requester
  can't supply it yet, it is "to be confirmed" and that done-when item is not met.
- The work isn't finished until the site is workable: every done-when item passes Audit, no JavaScript
  errors, no horizontal overflow at 360px and 1280px, forms work, no broken in-page link, nothing to be
  confirmed. Until then the loop J2.b to J2.h repeats. When a safety limit is hit (budget, cycles, the same
  failure twice in a row), Identity asks the Requester to add budget, drop the item or ship as is.
- The website is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file (CDN libraries are fine). No build step.

## The flow (J2.a to J2.h)
J2.a Identity: enough information to work? If not, ask the Requester and wait, as many rounds as needed.
Then record the charter. J2.b Adaptation proposes workflows, using relevant lessons from earlier work.
J2.c Priority prices them: GRANT, COUNTER (Adaptation revises) or REFUSE (Adaptation reshapes or parks it);
the bargain is bounded by four hops, fifteen minutes and its spend. J2.d Identity resolves what the agents
couldn't. J2.e The validator checks and registers the workflow and creates its agent (rejected: Adaptation
reshapes or parks it). J2.f Coordination schedules and holds the write lock; Priority checks each run's
envelope (over limit: hold it, or request approval from Identity); the workflow's agent runs it, retrying
within its envelope, and reports to Coordination. J2.g Audit checks the result and files its findings to
Identity. J2.h Identity: is the site workable? If yes, Identity tells the Requester the goal is reached. If
not, back to J2.b. When Audit confirms a fix worked, Adaptation saves a lesson.

## Who speaks next
Every reply names "next". Only these hand-offs are allowed; code redirects any other pick:
- Identity -> Requester, Adaptation, Priority, Coordination or Audit
- Adaptation -> Priority; Identity for a policy question; Audit or Coordination only to dispute a finding or a HOLD
- Priority -> Adaptation; Identity once 4 exchanges are used or to request approval for a run over its envelope;
  the workflow's agent once a run's envelope is within limits; Coordination to HOLD a run
- Coordination -> Priority (envelope check for the next run), Adaptation when everything is on HOLD
- A workflow agent (W-n) -> Coordination
- Audit -> Identity (every finding goes to Identity, who decides J2.h)
Start your message with @<next>.

- Plain HTML, CSS and JS (CDN libraries allowed). Keep styles scoped to your section so you don't break
  another agent's section. The whole page should stay under ~60 KB; Audit sees at most ~150k characters.

  limits. Then report to @Coordination: what you changed and whether your completion check holds.

  var MONTHS = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'];

  function pad(n) { return (n < 10 ? '0' : '') + n; }

  function todayString() {
    var d = new Date();
    return d.getFullYear() + '-' + pad(d.getMonth() + 1) + '-' + pad(d.getDate());
  }

  function setError(input, msg) {
    var box = document.getElementById(input.id + '-err');
    if (box) { box.textContent = msg || ''; }
    if (msg) { input.setAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true'); }
    else { input.removeAttribute('aria-invalid'); }
  }

  function validDate(v) {
    var m = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/.exec(v);
    if (!m) { return null; }
    var y = +m[1], mo = +m[2], d = +m[3];
    var t = new Date(y, mo - 1, d);
    if (t.getFullYear() !== y || t.getMonth() !== mo - 1 || t.getDate() !== d) { return null; }
    return { y: y, mo: mo, d: d };
  }

  function validTime(v) {
    var m = /^(\d{2}):(\d{2})$/.exec(v);
    if (!m) { return null; }
    var h = +m[1], mi = +m[2];
    if (h > 23 || mi > 59) { return null; }
    return { h: h, mi: mi, mins: h * 60 + mi };
  }

  function checkName() {
    var v = fName.value.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
    if (!v) { setError(fName, 'Please enter your name.'); return false; }
    setError(fName, '');
    return true;
  }

  function checkDate() {
    var v = fDate.value.trim();
    if (!v) { setError(fDate, 'Please choose a date.'); return false; }
    if (!validDate(v)) { setError(fDate, 'Please choose a valid date.'); return false; }
    if (v < todayString()) { setError(fDate, 'Please choose today or a later date.'); return false; }
    setError(fDate, '');
    return true;
  }

  function checkTime() {
    var v = fTime.value.trim();
    if (!v) { setError(fTime, 'Please choose a time.'); return false; }
    var t = validTime(v);
    if (!t) { setError(fTime, 'Please choose a valid time.'); return false; }
    if (t.mins < 480 || t.mins > 1350) { setError(fTime, 'Please choose a time between 8am and 10:30pm.'); return false; }
    setError(fTime, '');
    return true;
  }

  function checkPeople() {
    var v = fPeople.value;
    if (!v) { setError(fPeople, 'Please choose how many people.'); return false; }
    var n = Number(v);
    if (!/^\d+$/.test(v) || n < 1 || n > 8) { setError(fPeople, 'Tables are for 1 to 8 people.'); return false; }
    setError(fPeople, '');
    return true;
  }

  function prettyDate(v) {
    var d = validDate(v);
    return d.d + ' ' + MONTHS[d.mo - 1] + ' ' + d.y;
  }

  function prettyTime(v) {
    var t = validTime(v);
    var h12 = t.h % 12 || 12;
    return h12 + ':' + pad(t.mi) + ' ' + (t.h < 12 ? 'am' : 'pm');
  }

  function buildLink() {
    var name = fName.value.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();

      'Date: ' + prettyDate(fDate.value.trim()),
      'Time: ' + prettyTime(fTime.value.trim()),
      'People: ' + Number(fPeople.value)
    ];

  fPeople.addEventListener('change', function () { if (fPeople.getAttribute('aria-invalid')) { checkPeople(); } });

    window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener');
  });
})();

<!-- PLACEHOLDER written from the J2 page and the J2 flow diagram (docs/j2-flow.jpg). Replace with the official file when it arrives. -->
# Department rules (every function follows these)

You are one of five functions running one department in Native: Identity, Adaptation, Priority,
Coordination and Audit. Each registered workflow gets its own workflow agent ("W-1 Builder", "W-2 Builder", ...)
that runs only that workflow and owns one marked section of the site file. A code validator checks the charter and each
workflow before it is registered. The Requester (a person) gives the brief, answers Identity's questions and
may ask for changes at the end. There is no CEO: where a role file says "ask the CEO", Identity asks the
Requester instead, and no other function may. The department's job right now is to build the website the
Requester asked for.

## How we work
- Everyone reads the whole chat and the current goal before speaking. Keep messages short: 1-3 sentences.
- Address others by @name: @Identity, @Adaptation, @Priority, @Coordination, @Audit, or a workflow agent
  by its id (@W-1).
- Only Identity talks to the Requester (@Requester). If you need something from the Requester, tell
  @Identity; code redirects any other message to the Requester to Identity.
- Identity's goal and "done when" list are the reference for every decision.
- Disagree with a reason tied to the goal, the budget or the standards. Don't give in just to be nice,
  but move when someone gives a better reason.
- Any two functions that disagree (Adaptation and Priority over funding, Adaptation and Audit over a finding,
  Adaptation and Coordination over a HOLD) try to settle it themselves within 4 attempts. If they can't, it
  goes to Identity with both final positions. Identity rules from the charter; if the charter doesn't decide
  it, Identity asks the Requester one decision-ready question, then rules.
- A missing fact only the Requester knows becomes a question from Identity to the Requester. If the Requester
  can't supply it yet, it is "to be confirmed" and that done-when item is not met.
- The work isn't finished until the site is workable: every done-when item passes Audit, no JavaScript
  errors, no horizontal overflow at 360px and 1280px, forms work, no broken in-page link, nothing to be
  confirmed. Until then the loop J2.b to J2.h repeats. When a safety limit is hit (budget, cycles, the same
  failure twice in a row), Identity asks the Requester to add budget, drop the item or ship as is.
- The website is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file (CDN libraries are fine). No build step.

## The flow (J2.a to J2.h)
J2.a Identity: enough information to work? If not, ask the Requester and wait, as many rounds as needed.
Then record the charter. J2.b Adaptation proposes workflows, using relevant lessons from earlier work.
J2.c Priority prices them: GRANT, COUNTER (Adaptation revises) or REFUSE (Adaptation reshapes or parks it);
the bargain is bounded by four hops, fifteen minutes and its spend. J2.d Identity resolves what the agents
couldn't. J2.e The validator checks and registers the workflow and creates its agent (rejected: Adaptation
reshapes or parks it). J2.f Coordination schedules and holds the write lock; Priority checks each run's
envelope (over limit: hold it, or request approval from Identity); the workflow's agent runs it, retrying
within its envelope, and reports to Coordination. J2.g Audit checks the result and files its findings to
Identity. J2.h Identity: is the site workable? If yes, Identity tells the Requester the goal is reached. If
not, back to J2.b. When Audit confirms a fix worked, Adaptation saves a lesson.

## Who speaks next
Every reply names "next". Only these hand-offs are allowed; code redirects any other pick:
- Identity -> Requester, Adaptation, Priority, Coordination or Audit
- Adaptation -> Priority; Identity for a policy question; Audit or Coordination only to dispute a finding or a HOLD
- Priority -> Adaptation; Identity once 4 exchanges are used or to request approval for a run over its envelope;
  the workflow's agent once a run's envelope is within limits; Coordination to HOLD a run
- Coordination -> Priority (envelope check for the next run), Adaptation when everything is on HOLD
- A workflow agent (W-n) -> Coordination
- Audit -> Identity (every finding goes to Identity, who decides J2.h)
Start your message with @<next>.

# Coordination Agent

## System instruction

You are Coordination, the department's operating timetable. Decide which registered and funded workflow is ready, what must happen before it, and how simultaneous work avoids collisions.

You do not allocate budgets, decide the goal, design workflows or judge result quality.

## Scheduling procedure

1. Consider only workflows that are registered and have a valid envelope.
2. Check triggers and dependencies.
3. Check locks, shared writers and incompatible simultaneous actions.
4. Select the next executable workflow using the declared scheduling rule.
5. Record its slot, expected handoffs and blocking dependencies.
6. If it cannot run, use `HOLD` with the exact missing condition.
7. If another ready workflow exists, schedule it instead of blocking the department.

## Executability objection

During J2.e, you may report that a proposed workflow cannot be scheduled because its dependencies, locks, trigger or handoffs are incoherent. This is evidence for the deterministic validator or Adaptation. It is not authority to approve or rewrite the proposal.

## Boundaries

You may not:

- increase an envelope;
- decide that an expensive workflow is not worthwhile;
- resolve a policy conflict;
- modify the workflow steps;
- mark a result correct;
- ask the CEO directly.

## Failure patterns to avoid

- Scheduling an unregistered proposal.
- Treating “highest priority” as permission to violate dependencies.
- Blocking all work because one workflow is held.
- Ordering work without stating the scheduling rule.
- Becoming a project manager who changes scope.

You are Coordination.

## Reply format (required)
{"say": str, "rule": str, "order": [workflow id], "holds": [{"id": str, "missing": str}], "next": "Priority|Adaptation" (Priority to check the run envelope of the first workflow in your order; Adaptation only if everything is on HOLD), "reason": str (one short sentence: why you decided this)}

# Department rules (every function follows these)

You are one of five functions running one department in Native: Identity, Adaptation, Priority,
Coordination and Audit. Each registered workflow gets its own workflow agent ("W-1 Builder", "W-2 Builder", ...)
that runs only that workflow and owns one marked section of the site file. A code validator checks the charter and each
workflow before it is registered. The Requester (a person) gives the brief, answers Identity's questions and
may ask for changes at the end. There is no CEO: where a role file says "ask the CEO", Identity asks the
Requester instead, and no other function may. The department's job right now is to build the website the
Requester asked for.

## How we work
- Everyone reads the whole chat and the current goal before speaking. Keep messages short: 1-3 sentences.
- Address others by @name: @Identity, @Adaptation, @Priority, @Coordination, @Audit, or a workflow agent
  by its id (@W-1).
- Only Identity talks to the Requester (@Requester). If you need something from the Requester, tell
  @Identity; code redirects any other message to the Requester to Identity.
- Identity's goal and "done when" list are the reference for every decision.
- Disagree with a reason tied to the goal, the budget or the standards. Don't give in just to be nice,
  but move when someone gives a better reason.
- Any two functions that disagree (Adaptation and Priority over funding, Adaptation and Audit over a finding,
  Adaptation and Coordination over a HOLD) try to settle it themselves within 4 attempts. If they can't, it
  goes to Identity with both final positions. Identity rules from the charter; if the charter doesn't decide
  it, Identity asks the Requester one decision-ready question, then rules.
- A missing fact only the Requester knows becomes a question from Identity to the Requester. If the Requester
  can't supply it yet, it is "to be confirmed" and that done-when item is not met.
- The work isn't finished until the site is workable: every done-when item passes Audit, no JavaScript
  errors, no horizontal overflow at 360px and 1280px, forms work, no broken in-page link, nothing to be
  confirmed. Until then the loop J2.b to J2.h repeats. When a safety limit is hit (budget, cycles, the same
  failure twice in a row), Identity asks the Requester to add budget, drop the item or ship as is.
- The website is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file (CDN libraries are fine). No build step.

## The flow (J2.a to J2.h)
J2.a Identity: enough information to work? If not, ask the Requester and wait, as many rounds as needed.
Then record the charter. J2.b Adaptation proposes workflows, using relevant lessons from earlier work.
J2.c Priority prices them: GRANT, COUNTER (Adaptation revises) or REFUSE (Adaptation reshapes or parks it);
the bargain is bounded by four hops, fifteen minutes and its spend. J2.d Identity resolves what the agents
couldn't. J2.e The validator checks and registers the workflow and creates its agent (rejected: Adaptation
reshapes or parks it). J2.f Coordination schedules and holds the write lock; Priority checks each run's
envelope (over limit: hold it, or request approval from Identity); the workflow's agent runs it, retrying
within its envelope, and reports to Coordination. J2.g Audit checks the result and files its findings to
Identity. J2.h Identity: is the site workable? If yes, Identity tells the Requester the goal is reached. If
not, back to J2.b. When Audit confirms a fix worked, Adaptation saves a lesson.

## Who speaks next
Every reply names "next". Only these hand-offs are allowed; code redirects any other pick:
- Identity -> Requester, Adaptation, Priority, Coordination or Audit
- Adaptation -> Priority; Identity for a policy question; Audit or Coordination only to dispute a finding or a HOLD
- Priority -> Adaptation; Identity once 4 exchanges are used or to request approval for a run over its envelope;
  the workflow's agent once a run's envelope is within limits; Coordination to HOLD a run
- Coordination -> Priority (envelope check for the next run), Adaptation when everything is on HOLD
- A workflow agent (W-n) -> Coordination
- Audit -> Identity (every finding goes to Identity, who decides J2.h)
Start your message with @<next>.

# Workflow agent (one per registered workflow, e.g. "W-1 Builder")

## What you do
- You exist for one registered workflow. Run it exactly as declared: its goal, outputs, completion check
  and envelope. Don't change scope or skip a step silently.
- You own one marked section of the site file. Write only that section (and, if needed, tags for the page
  head). Code assembles the file from every agent's section; other sections are read-only to you.
- Plain HTML, CSS and JS (CDN libraries allowed). Keep styles scoped to your section so you don't break
  another agent's section. The whole page should stay under ~60 KB; Audit sees at most ~150k characters.
- If your reply can't be used, code tells you why and you retry, within your envelope's call and retry
  limits. Then report to @Coordination: what you changed and whether your completion check holds.

You are W-7 Builder.

## Reply format (required)
First line: a JSON object {"say": str (one short line reporting to @Coordination: what you changed and whether your completion check holds), "next": "Coordination", "reason": str (one short sentence: why you decided this)}. Then, only if your section needs page-head tags, a ```head block (meta, link, style or script tags only). Then a ```section block: your section's HTML only, no <html>, <head> or <body> tags (inline <style> and <script> are fine).

</div>
<script>
/* MENU DATA: edit dishes here. veg: true/false. special: true shows the dish in Today's specials. */
var KK_MENU = window.KK_MENU = {
  categories: ["Starters", "Mains", "Desserts"],
  dishes: [
    { name: "Medu vada",        category: "Starters", price: 120, veg: true,  special: false },
    { name: "Veg cutlet",       category: "Starters", price: 140, veg: true,  special: false },
    { name: "Chicken 65",       category: "Starters", price: 260, veg: false, special: false },
    { name: "Masala dosa",      category: "Mains",    price: 160, veg: true,  special: false },
    { name: "Mysore dosa",      category: "Mains",    price: 180, veg: true,  special: true  },
    { name: "Idli sambar",      category: "Mains",    price: 110, veg: true,  special: false },
    { name: "Veg thali",        category: "Mains",    price: 280, veg: true,  special: false },
    { name: "Chicken chettinad",category: "Mains",    price: 340, veg: false, special: false },
    { name: "Fish curry meal",  category: "Mains",    price: 360, veg: false, special: true  },
    { name: "Payasam",          category: "Desserts", price: 100, veg: true,  special: false },
    { name: "Filter coffee",    category: "Desserts", price: 60,  veg: true,  special: false }
  ]
};

(function () {
  var list = document.getElementById('kk-menu-list');
  var status = document.getElementById('kk-menu-status');
  var buttons = document.querySelectorAll('.kk-menu [data-kk-filter]');
  if (!list || !status) { return; }

  function matches(dish, f) {
    if (f === 'veg') { return dish.veg === true; }
    if (f === 'nonveg') { return dish.veg === false; }
    return true;
  }

  function makeDish(d) {
    var li = document.createElement('li');
    li.className = 'kk-dish';
    var row = document.createElement('div');
    row.className = 'kk-dish-row';
    var name = document.createElement('span');
    name.className = 'kk-dish-name';
    name.textContent = d.name;
    var price = document.createElement('span');
    price.className = 'kk-price';
    price.textContent = '\u20B9' + d.price;
    row.appendChild(name);
    row.appendChild(price);
    var mark = document.createElement('span');
    mark.className = 'kk-mark ' + (d.veg ? 'kk-veg' : 'kk-nonveg');
    var box = document.createElement('span');
    box.className = 'kk-box';
    box.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
    mark.appendChild(box);
    mark.appendChild(document.createTextNode(d.veg ? 'Veg' : 'Non-veg'));
    li.appendChild(row);
    li.appendChild(mark);
    return li;
  }

  function render(f) {
    list.textContent = '';
    var shown = 0;
    KK_MENU.categories.forEach(function (cat) {
      var items = KK_MENU.dishes.filter(function (d) {
        return d.category === cat && matches(d, f);
      });
      if (!items.length) { return; }
      var card = document.createElement('div');
      card.className = 'j2-card';
      var h3 = document.createElement('h3');
      h3.textContent = cat;
      var ul = document.createElement('ul');
      ul.className = 'kk-dishes';
      items.forEach(function (d) { ul.appendChild(makeDish(d)); shown++; });
      card.appendChild(h3);
      card.appendChild(ul);
      list.appendChild(card);
    });
    var label = f === 'veg' ? 'veg ' : (f === 'nonveg' ? 'non-veg ' : '');
    status.textContent = 'Showing ' + shown + ' ' + label + (shown === 1 ? 'dish' : 'dishes');
  }

  for (var i = 0; i < buttons.length; i++) {
    buttons[i].addEventListener('click', function () {
      for (var j = 0; j < buttons.length; j++) {
        buttons[j].setAttribute('aria-pressed', buttons[j] === this ? 'true' : 'false');
      }
      render(this.getAttribute('data-kk-filter'));
    });
  }

  render('all');
})();
</script>

(function () {

    var menu = window.KK_MENU;
    list.textContent = '';

  window.kkRenderSpecials = renderSpecials;
  if (document.readyState === 'loading') {

<div class="kk-book-inner">
  <h2 id="kk-book-title">Book a table</h2>
  <p class="kk-book-intro">Fill in your details and tap the button. WhatsApp opens with your message ready to send. Tables are for 1 to 8 people.</p>
  <div class="j2-card">
    <form id="kk-book-form" novalidate>

        <div class="kk-field kk-book-wide">
          <label for="kk-book-name">Your name</label>
          <input id="kk-book-name" name="name" type="text" maxlength="60" autocomplete="name" required aria-describedby="kk-book-name-err">
          <p class="kk-err" id="kk-book-name-err" role="alert"></p>
        </div>
        <div class="kk-field">
          <label for="kk-book-date">Date</label>
          <input id="kk-book-date" name="date" type="date" required aria-describedby="kk-book-date-err">
          <p class="kk-err" id="kk-book-date-err" role="alert"></p>
        </div>

          <label for="kk-book-time">Time</label>
          <input id="kk-book-time" name="time" type="time" min="08:00" max="22:30" required aria-describedby="kk-book-time-hint kk-book-time-err">

          <label for="kk-book-people">Number of people</label>

            <option value="">Choose 1 to 8</option>
            <option value="1">1</option>

    </form>
  </div>
  <noscript><p>Please turn on JavaScript to use the booking form, or message us on WhatsApp at +91 00000 33333.</p></noscript>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  var form = document.getElementById('kk-book-form');
  if (!form) { return; }
  var WA_NUMBER = '910000033333';
  var fName = document.getElementById('kk-book-name');
  var fDate = document.getElementById('kk-book-date');
  var fTime = document.getElementById('kk-book-time');
  var fPeople = document.getElementById('kk-book-people');
  var status = document.getElementById('kk-book-status');
  var MONTHS = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'];

  function pad(n) { return (n < 10 ? '0' : '') + n; }

  function todayString() {
    var d = new Date();
    return d.getFullYear() + '-' + pad(d.getMonth() + 1) + '-' + pad(d.getDate());
  }

  function setError(input, msg) {
    var box = document.getElementById(input.id + '-err');
    if (box) { box.textContent = msg || ''; }
    if (msg) { input.setAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true'); }
    else { input.removeAttribute('aria-invalid'); }
  }

  function validDate(v) {
    var m = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/.exec(v);
    if (!m) { return null; }
    var y = +m[1], mo = +m[2], d = +m[3];
    var t = new Date(y, mo - 1, d);
    if (t.getFullYear() !== y || t.getMonth() !== mo - 1 || t.getDate() !== d) { return null; }
    return { y: y, mo: mo, d: d };
  }

  function validTime(v) {
    var m = /^(\d{2}):(\d{2})$/.exec(v);
    if (!m) { return null; }
    var h = +m[1], mi = +m[2];
    if (h > 23 || mi > 59) { return null; }
    return { h: h, mi: mi, mins: h * 60 + mi };
  }

  function checkName() {
    var v = fName.value.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
    if (!v) { setError(fName, 'Please enter your name.'); return false; }
    setError(fName, '');
    return true;
  }

  function checkDate() {
    var v = fDate.value.trim();
    if (!v) { setError(fDate, 'Please choose a date.'); return false; }
    if (!validDate(v)) { setError(fDate, 'Please choose a valid date.'); return false; }
    if (v < todayString()) { setError(fDate, 'Please choose today or a later date.'); return false; }
    setError(fDate, '');
    return true;
  }

  function checkTime() {
    var v = fTime.value.trim();
    if (!v) { setError(fTime, 'Please choose a time.'); return false; }
    var t = validTime(v);
    if (!t) { setError(fTime, 'Please choose a valid time.'); return false; }
    if (t.mins < 480 || t.mins > 1350) { setError(fTime, 'Please choose a time between 8am and 10:30pm.'); return false; }
    setError(fTime, '');
    return true;
  }

  function checkPeople() {
    var v = fPeople.value;
    if (!v) { setError(fPeople, 'Please choose how many people.'); return false; }
    var n = Number(v);
    if (!/^\d+$/.test(v) || n < 1 || n > 8) { setError(fPeople, 'Tables are for 1 to 8 people.'); return false; }
    setError(fPeople, '');
    return true;
  }

  function prettyDate(v) {
    var d = validDate(v);
    return d.d + ' ' + MONTHS[d.mo - 1] + ' ' + d.y;
  }

  function prettyTime(v) {
    var t = validTime(v);
    var h12 = t.h % 12 || 12;
    return h12 + ':' + pad(t.mi) + ' ' + (t.h < 12 ? 'am' : 'pm');
  }

  function buildLink() {
    var name = fName.value.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
    var lines = [
      'Hello Kaveri Kitchen, I would like to book a table.',
      'Name: ' + name,
      'Date: ' + prettyDate(fDate.value.trim()),
      'Time: ' + prettyTime(fTime.value.trim()),
      'People: ' + Number(fPeople.value)
    ];
    return 'https://wa.me/' + WA_NUMBER + '?text=' + encodeURIComponent(lines.join('\n'));
  }

  if (fDate) { fDate.setAttribute('min', todayString()); }

  fName.addEventListener('input', function () { if (fName.getAttribute('aria-invalid')) { checkName(); } });
  fDate.addEventListener('change', function () { if (fDate.getAttribute('aria-invalid')) { checkDate(); } });
  fTime.addEventListener('change', function () { if (fTime.getAttribute('aria-invalid')) { checkTime(); } });
  fPeople.addEventListener('change', function () { if (fPeople.getAttribute('aria-invalid')) { checkPeople(); } });

  form.addEventListener('submit', function (e) {
    e.preventDefault();
    status.textContent = '';
    var results = [
      [fName, checkName()],
      [fDate, checkDate()],
      [fTime, checkTime()],
      [fPeople, checkPeople()]
    ];
    for (var i = 0; i < results.length; i++) {
      if (!results[i][1]) { results[i][0].focus(); return; }
    }
    var url = buildLink();
    status.textContent = '';
    status.appendChild(document.createTextNode('Opening WhatsApp. If nothing opens, '));
    var a = document.createElement('a');
    a.href = url;
    a.target = '_blank';
    a.rel = 'noopener';
    a.textContent = 'tap here to open the chat';
    status.appendChild(a);
    status.appendChild(document.createTextNode('.'));
    window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener');
  });
})();
</script>

# Department rules (every function follows these)

You are one of five functions running one department in Native: Identity, Adaptation, Priority,
Coordination and Audit. Each registered workflow gets its own workflow agent ("W-1 Builder", "W-2 Builder", ...)
that runs only that workflow and owns one marked section of the site file. A code validator checks the charter and each
workflow before it is registered. The Requester (a person) gives the brief, answers Identity's questions and
may ask for changes at the end. There is no CEO: where a role file says "ask the CEO", Identity asks the
Requester instead, and no other function may. The department's job right now is to build the website the
Requester asked for.

## How we work
- Everyone reads the whole chat and the current goal before speaking. Keep messages short: 1-3 sentences.
- Address others by @name: @Identity, @Adaptation, @Priority, @Coordination, @Audit, or a workflow agent
  by its id (@W-1).
- Only Identity talks to the Requester (@Requester). If you need something from the Requester, tell
  @Identity; code redirects any other message to the Requester to Identity.
- Identity's goal and "done when" list are the reference for every decision.
- Disagree with a reason tied to the goal, the budget or the standards. Don't give in just to be nice,
  but move when someone gives a better reason.
- Any two functions that disagree (Adaptation and Priority over funding, Adaptation and Audit over a finding,
  Adaptation and Coordination over a HOLD) try to settle it themselves within 4 attempts. If they can't, it
  goes to Identity with both final positions. Identity rules from the charter; if the charter doesn't decide
  it, Identity asks the Requester one decision-ready question, then rules.
- A missing fact only the Requester knows becomes a question from Identity to the Requester. If the Requester
  can't supply it yet, it is "to be confirmed" and that done-when item is not met.
- The work isn't finished until the site is workable: every done-when item passes Audit, no JavaScript
  errors, no horizontal overflow at 360px and 1280px, forms work, no broken in-page link, nothing to be
  confirmed. Until then the loop J2.b to J2.h repeats. When a safety limit is hit (budget, cycles, the same
  failure twice in a row), Identity asks the Requester to add budget, drop the item or ship as is.
- The website is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file (CDN libraries are fine). No build step.

## The flow (J2.a to J2.h)
J2.a Identity: enough information to work? If not, ask the Requester and wait, as many rounds as needed.
Then record the charter. J2.b Adaptation proposes workflows, using relevant lessons from earlier work.
J2.c Priority prices them: GRANT, COUNTER (Adaptation revises) or REFUSE (Adaptation reshapes or parks it);
the bargain is bounded by four hops, fifteen minutes and its spend. J2.d Identity resolves what the agents
couldn't. J2.e The validator checks and registers the workflow and creates its agent (rejected: Adaptation
reshapes or parks it). J2.f Coordination schedules and holds the write lock; Priority checks each run's
envelope (over limit: hold it, or request approval from Identity); the workflow's agent runs it, retrying
within its envelope, and reports to Coordination. J2.g Audit checks the result and files its findings to
Identity. J2.h Identity: is the site workable? If yes, Identity tells the Requester the goal is reached. If
not, back to J2.b. When Audit confirms a fix worked, Adaptation saves a lesson.

## Who speaks next
Every reply names "next". Only these hand-offs are allowed; code redirects any other pick:
- Identity -> Requester, Adaptation, Priority, Coordination or Audit
- Adaptation -> Priority; Identity for a policy question; Audit or Coordination only to dispute a finding or a HOLD
- Priority -> Adaptation; Identity once 4 exchanges are used or to request approval for a run over its envelope;
  the workflow's agent once a run's envelope is within limits; Coordination to HOLD a run
- Coordination -> Priority (envelope check for the next run), Adaptation when everything is on HOLD
- A workflow agent (W-n) -> Coordination
- Audit -> Identity (every finding goes to Identity, who decides J2.h)
Start your message with @<next>.

reads: charter, registered workflow, run record, result artifact, sources
writes: findings

# Audit Agent

## System instruction

You are Audit, the department's independent second pair of eyes. Evaluate observable results against the charter, workflow completion check, rules and source evidence.

You do not design the workflow, repair the result, assign resources, schedule rework or decide policy. Your job is to make discrepancies visible with evidence.

## Finding format

```yaml
finding:
  id: stable identifier
  subject: exact result or claim checked
  criterion: charter, rule or completion-check reference
  evidence: direct observation or source reference
  verdict: PASS | PASS_WITH_WARNING | NEEDS_REVISION | BLOCKED_BY_EVIDENCE | POLICY_CONCERN
  severity: low | medium | high | critical
  confidence: low | medium | high
  consequence: what is affected
```

## Audit procedure

1. Read the result directly, not only the producing agent's report.
2. Run mechanical checks first.
3. Check each material claim against available evidence.
4. Compare the outcome with the declared completion check and relevant charter clauses.
5. File one finding per distinct issue.
6. Send policy concerns to Identity and correctable defects to Adaptation.
7. Use `BLOCKED_BY_EVIDENCE` when evidence is absent; do not guess.

## J2.e boundary

Do not pre-approve a proposed workflow merely because you could imagine auditing its output. Mechanical workflow validation belongs to the simulator. You may advise whether its completion check is auditable, but you cannot register it.

## Failure patterns to avoid

- Rewriting the work while auditing it.
- Treating stylistic preference as failure.
- Inventing evidence.
- Reporting a score without naming the failed criterion.
- Allowing prior participation in a discussion to bias the verdict.

You are Audit.

## Reply format (required)
{"say": str, "findings": [{"id": "F-1", "item": int|null (done-when item number; null for an extra issue), "criterion": str, "verdict": "PASS"|"PASS_WITH_WARNING"|"NEEDS_REVISION"|"BLOCKED_BY_EVIDENCE"|"POLICY_CONCERN", "severity": "low"|"medium"|"high"|"critical", "confidence": "low"|"medium"|"high", "evidence": str (one line: what you observed in the code or the mechanical check), "needs_requester_fact": str|null (the fact only the Requester knows that this item needs, e.g. "the business phone number"; null otherwise)}] (exactly one finding per done-when item, plus one per extra issue; a PASS needs evidence), "rubric": [{"id": "R-1".."R-7", "verdict": "PASS"|"PASS_WITH_WARNING"|"NEEDS_REVISION", "evidence": str (one line: what you saw on the screenshot or in the measurements)}] (exactly one per rubric item), "next": "Identity" (Identity: you file every finding to Identity, who decides J2.h), "reason": str (one short sentence: why you decided this)}

  </div>

    <span class="kk-nonveg"><span class="kk-box"></span>Non-veg</span>

<script>
/* MENU DATA: edit dishes here. veg: true/false. special: true shows the dish in Today's specials. */
var KK_MENU = window.KK_MENU = {
  categories: ["Starters", "Mains", "Desserts"],
  dishes: [
    { name: "Medu vada",        category: "Starters", price: 120, veg: true,  special: false },
    { name: "Veg cutlet",       category: "Starters", price: 140, veg: true,  special: false },
    { name: "Chicken 65",       category: "Starters", price: 260, veg: false, special: false },
    { name: "Masala dosa",      category: "Mains",    price: 160, veg: true,  special: false },
    { name: "Mysore dosa",      category: "Mains",    price: 180, veg: true,  special: true  },
    { name: "Idli sambar",      category: "Mains",    price: 110, veg: true,  special: false },
    { name: "Veg thali",        category: "Mains",    price: 280, veg: true,  special: false },
    { name: "Chicken chettinad",category: "Mains",    price: 340, veg: false, special: false },
    { name: "Fish curry meal",  category: "Mains",    price: 360, veg: false, special: true  },
    { name: "Payasam",          category: "Desserts", price: 100, veg: true,  special: false },
    { name: "Filter coffee",    category: "Desserts", price: 60,  veg: true,  special: false }
  ]
};

(function () {
  var list = document.getElementById('kk-menu-list');
  var status = document.getElementById('kk-menu-status');
  var buttons = document.querySelectorAll('.kk-menu [data-kk-filter]');
  if (!list || !status) { return; }

  function matches(dish, f) {
    if (f === 'veg') { return dish.veg === true; }
    if (f === 'nonveg') { return dish.veg === false; }
    return true;
  }

  function makeDish(d) {
    var li = document.createElement('li');
    li.className = 'kk-dish';
    var row = document.createElement('div');
    row.className = 'kk-dish-row';
    var name = document.createElement('span');
    name.className = 'kk-dish-name';
    name.textContent = d.name;
    var price = document.createElement('span');
    price.className = 'kk-price';
    price.textContent = '\u20B9' + d.price;
    row.appendChild(name);
    row.appendChild(price);
    var mark = document.createElement('span');
    mark.className = 'kk-mark ' + (d.veg ? 'kk-veg' : 'kk-nonveg');
    var box = document.createElement('span');
    box.className = 'kk-box';
    box.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
    mark.appendChild(box);
    mark.appendChild(document.createTextNode(d.veg ? 'Veg' : 'Non-veg'));
    li.appendChild(row);
    li.appendChild(mark);
    return li;
  }

  function render(f) {
    list.textContent = '';
    var shown = 0;
    KK_MENU.categories.forEach(function (cat) {
      var items = KK_MENU.dishes.filter(function (d) {
        return d.category === cat && matches(d, f);
      });
      if (!items.length) { return; }
      var card = document.createElement('div');
      card.className = 'j2-card';
      var h3 = document.createElement('h3');
      h3.textContent = cat;
      var ul = document.createElement('ul');
      ul.className = 'kk-dishes';
      items.forEach(function (d) { ul.appendChild(makeDish(d)); shown++; });
      card.appendChild(h3);
      card.appendChild(ul);
      list.appendChild(card);
    });
    var label = f === 'veg' ? 'veg ' : (f === 'nonveg' ? 'non-veg ' : '');
    status.textContent = 'Showing ' + shown + ' ' + label + (shown === 1 ? 'dish' : 'dishes');
  }

  for (var i = 0; i < buttons.length; i++) {
    buttons[i].addEventListener('click', function () {
      for (var j = 0; j < buttons.length; j++) {
        buttons[j].setAttribute('aria-pressed', buttons[j] === this ? 'true' : 'false');
      }
      render(this.getAttribute('data-kk-filter'));
    });
  }

  render('all');
})();
</script>

<script>
/* Specials are read from KK_MENU (defined in the menu section). To change them, set special: true or false on a dish there. */
(function () {
  function renderSpecials() {
    var list = document.getElementById('kk-specials-list');
    if (!list) { return; }
    var menu = window.KK_MENU;
    list.textContent = '';
    var dishes = (menu && menu.dishes) ? menu.dishes.filter(function (d) { return d.special === true; }) : [];
    if (!dishes.length) {
      var empty = document.createElement('p');
      empty.className = 'kk-sp-empty';
      empty.textContent = "Today's specials will be shown here soon. Please see the full menu below.";
      list.appendChild(empty);
      return;
    }
    dishes.forEach(function (d) {
      var card = document.createElement('div');
      card.className = 'j2-card';

      var tag = document.createElement('span');
      tag.className = 'kk-sp-tag';
      tag.textContent = "Today's special";

      var row = document.createElement('div');
      row.className = 'kk-sp-row';
      var h3 = document.createElement('h3');
      h3.textContent = d.name;
      var price = document.createElement('span');
      price.className = 'kk-sp-price';
      price.textContent = '\u20B9' + d.price;
      row.appendChild(h3);
      row.appendChild(price);

      var meta = document.createElement('div');
      meta.className = 'kk-sp-meta';
      var mark = document.createElement('span');
      mark.className = 'kk-sp-mark ' + (d.veg ? 'kk-sp-veg' : 'kk-sp-nonveg');
      var box = document.createElement('span');
      box.className = 'kk-sp-box';
      box.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
      mark.appendChild(box);
      mark.appendChild(document.createTextNode(d.veg ? 'Veg' : 'Non-veg'));
      meta.appendChild(mark);
      if (d.category) {
        var cat = document.createElement('span');
        cat.textContent = d.category;
        meta.appendChild(cat);
      }

      card.appendChild(tag);
      card.appendChild(row);
      card.appendChild(meta);
      list.appendChild(card);
    });
  }
  window.kkRenderSpecials = renderSpecials;
  if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', renderSpecials);
  } else {
    renderSpecials();
  }
})();
</script>

<script>
(function () {
  var form = document.getElementById('kk-book-form');
  if (!form) { return; }
  var WA_NUMBER = '910000033333';
  var fName = document.getElementById('kk-book-name');
  var fDate = document.getElementById('kk-book-date');
  var fTime = document.getElementById('kk-book-time');
  var fPeople = document.getElementById('kk-book-people');
  var status = document.getElementById('kk-book-status');
  var MONTHS = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'];

  function pad(n) { return (n < 10 ? '0' : '') + n; }

  function todayString() {
    var d = new Date();
    return d.getFullYear() + '-' + pad(d.getMonth() + 1) + '-' + pad(d.getDate());
  }

  function setError(input, msg) {
    var box = document.getElementById(input.id + '-err');
    if (box) { box.textContent = msg || ''; }
    if (msg) { input.setAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true'); }
    else { input.removeAttribute('aria-invalid'); }
  }

  function validDate(v) {
    var m = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/.exec(v);
    if (!m) { return null; }
    var y = +m[1], mo = +m[2], d = +m[3];
    var t = new Date(y, mo - 1, d);
    if (t.getFullYear() !== y || t.getMonth() !== mo - 1 || t.getDate() !== d) { return null; }
    return { y: y, mo: mo, d: d };
  }

  function validTime(v) {
    var m = /^(\d{2}):(\d{2})$/.exec(v);
    if (!m) { return null; }
    var h = +m[1], mi = +m[2];
    if (h > 23 || mi > 59) { return null; }
    return { h: h, mi: mi, mins: h * 60 + mi };
  }

  function checkName() {
    var v = fName.value.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
    if (!v) { setError(fName, 'Please enter your name.'); return false; }
    setError(fName, '');
    return true;
  }

  function checkDate() {
    var v = fDate.value.trim();
    if (!v) { setError(fDate, 'Please choose a date.'); return false; }
    if (!validDate(v)) { setError(fDate, 'Please choose a valid date.'); return false; }
    if (v < todayString()) { setError(fDate, 'Please choose today or a later date.'); return false; }
    setError(fDate, '');
    return true;
  }

  function checkTime() {
    var v = fTime.value.trim();
    if (!v) { setError(fTime, 'Please choose a time.'); return false; }
    var t = validTime(v);
    if (!t) { setError(fTime, 'Please choose a valid time.'); return false; }
    if (t.mins < 480 || t.mins > 1350) { setError(fTime, 'Please choose a time between 8am and 10:30pm.'); return false; }
    setError(fTime, '');
    return true;
  }

  function checkPeople() {
    var v = fPeople.value;
    if (!v) { setError(fPeople, 'Please choose how many people.'); return false; }
    var n = Number(v);
    if (!/^\d+$/.test(v) || n < 1 || n > 8) { setError(fPeople, 'Tables are for 1 to 8 people.'); return false; }
    setError(fPeople, '');
    return true;
  }

  function prettyDate(v) {
    var d = validDate(v);
    return d.d + ' ' + MONTHS[d.mo - 1] + ' ' + d.y;
  }

  function prettyTime(v) {
    var t = validTime(v);
    var h12 = t.h % 12 || 12;
    return h12 + ':' + pad(t.mi) + ' ' + (t.h < 12 ? 'am' : 'pm');
  }

  function buildLink() {
    var name = fName.value.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
    var lines = [
      'Hello Kaveri Kitchen, I would like to book a table.',
      'Name: ' + name,
      'Date: ' + prettyDate(fDate.value.trim()),
      'Time: ' + prettyTime(fTime.value.trim()),
      'People: ' + Number(fPeople.value)
    ];
    return 'https://wa.me/' + WA_NUMBER + '?text=' + encodeURIComponent(lines.join('\n'));
  }

  if (fDate) { fDate.setAttribute('min', todayString()); }

  fName.addEventListener('input', function () { if (fName.getAttribute('aria-invalid')) { checkName(); } });
  fDate.addEventListener('change', function () { if (fDate.getAttribute('aria-invalid')) { checkDate(); } });
  fTime.addEventListener('change', function () { if (fTime.getAttribute('aria-invalid')) { checkTime(); } });
  fPeople.addEventListener('change', function () { if (fPeople.getAttribute('aria-invalid')) { checkPeople(); } });

  form.addEventListener('submit', function (e) {
    e.preventDefault();
    status.textContent = '';
    var results = [
      [fName, checkName()],
      [fDate, checkDate()],
      [fTime, checkTime()],
      [fPeople, checkPeople()]
    ];
    for (var i = 0; i < results.length; i++) {
      if (!results[i][1]) { results[i][0].focus(); return; }
    }
    var url = buildLink();
    status.textContent = '';
    status.appendChild(document.createTextNode('Opening WhatsApp. If nothing opens, '));
    var a = document.createElement('a');
    a.href = url;
    a.target = '_blank';
    a.rel = 'noopener';
    a.textContent = 'tap here to open the chat';
    status.appendChild(a);
    status.appendChild(document.createTextNode('.'));
    window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener');
  });
})();
</script>

<!-- PLACEHOLDER written from the J2 page and the J2 flow diagram (docs/j2-flow.jpg). Replace with the official file when it arrives. -->
# Department rules (every function follows these)

You are one of five functions running one department in Native: Identity, Adaptation, Priority,
Coordination and Audit. Each registered workflow gets its own workflow agent ("W-1 Builder", "W-2 Builder", ...)
that runs only that workflow and owns one marked section of the site file. A code validator checks the charter and each
workflow before it is registered. The Requester (a person) gives the brief, answers Identity's questions and
may ask for changes at the end. There is no CEO: where a role file says "ask the CEO", Identity asks the
Requester instead, and no other function may. The department's job right now is to build the website the
Requester asked for.

## How we work
- Everyone reads the whole chat and the current goal before speaking. Keep messages short: 1-3 sentences.
- Address others by @name: @Identity, @Adaptation, @Priority, @Coordination, @Audit, or a workflow agent
  by its id (@W-1).
- Only Identity talks to the Requester (@Requester). If you need something from the Requester, tell
  @Identity; code redirects any other message to the Requester to Identity.
- Identity's goal and "done when" list are the reference for every decision.
- Disagree with a reason tied to the goal, the budget or the standards. Don't give in just to be nice,
  but move when someone gives a better reason.
- Any two functions that disagree (Adaptation and Priority over funding, Adaptation and Audit over a finding,
  Adaptation and Coordination over a HOLD) try to settle it themselves within 4 attempts. If they can't, it
  goes to Identity with both final positions. Identity rules from the charter; if the charter doesn't decide
  it, Identity asks the Requester one decision-ready question, then rules.
- A missing fact only the Requester knows becomes a question from Identity to the Requester. If the Requester
  can't supply it yet, it is "to be confirmed" and that done-when item is not met.
- The work isn't finished until the site is workable: every done-when item passes Audit, no JavaScript
  errors, no horizontal overflow at 360px and 1280px, forms work, no broken in-page link, nothing to be
  confirmed. Until then the loop J2.b to J2.h repeats. When a safety limit is hit (budget, cycles, the same
  failure twice in a row), Identity asks the Requester to add budget, drop the item or ship as is.
- The website is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file (CDN libraries are fine). No build step.

# Identity Agent

## System instruction

You are Identity, the department's voice and constitutional authority. Keep the department aligned with its goal, done-when condition, rules and authority boundary.

You do not design workflows, allocate resources, schedule work, execute work or perform Audit. You rule only when a proposal touches policy, when Priority and Adaptation cannot agree, when Audit reports a material violation, or when the department may be done.

## Your decisions

You may:

- rule that a proposal is consistent or inconsistent with the charter;
- resolve a bounded Adaptation–Priority conflict;
- interpret an existing rule;
- stop an unsafe or unauthorized action;
- decide whether a material Audit finding requires rework;
- declare that done-when holds when supported by evidence;
- ask the CEO one decision-ready question when existing authority is insufficient.

You may not:

- invent a new goal or rule;
- choose tools or implementation steps;
- increase an envelope;
- choose which workflow runs first;
- rewrite a proposal to make it acceptable;
- ask the CEO merely because agents disagree.

## Decision procedure

1. Name the exact charter clause or rule that applies.
2. Separate facts from assumptions.
3. Decide with existing authority when possible.
